clue.text: Husband of Florence?

definitions.note: the whole clue stands for a man of Florence
definitions.meaning: the surface wants a married man; the setter only means a man
reads as a wife's name, but it is the Italian city, and the question mark admits the trick

explanation.walkthrough: The capital F makes Florence look like a wife's name, so you hunt for her husband; read it as the Italian city and any man from there is a Tuscan, since Florence is the capital of Tuscany.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by origin: anyone native to Florence, the Tuscan capital, is by region a Tuscan.

clue.text: Changes at home and goes to bed

parts.note: to change is to turn, as milk turns

explanation.surface: Someone potters about the house, switches outfits and heads upstairs for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'changes' as getting into pyjamas, but it is the verb turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn in is an informal way of saying to go to bed.

clue.text: Bog plant in small border

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A gardener plants something marshy in a narrow flower border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' tempts you to put something inside something, but here it only joins the definition to the wordplay, as in 'found in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant of wet, boggy ground.

clue.text: Fabulous time when we were so successful at the Olympics?

definitions.meaning: the golden age of myth and fable

definitions.text: when we were so successful at the Olympics?
definitions.note: a cryptic description of a period, read as a time
definitions.meaning: a spell of winning gold medals

explanation.surface: A nostalgic look back at the glory days when the national team kept winning Olympic medals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' here means belonging to fable: the mythical golden age. The second half is a playful reading, an age of gold medals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Age of Gold is the legendary era of Greek myth, and a run of Olympic golds would be one too.

clue.text: Tiny amount of French potage given to prisoner

parts.note: potage is the French word for soup

explanation.surface: A prisoner is served a meagre ladle of French soup.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a thin prison ration, and fittingly the answer is itself a French word for a tiny trace.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupçon is a very small amount, a hint or trace.

clue.text: Is angry, having to move shrub

indicators.note: the letters of IS ANGRY are told to move, so they change places

explanation.surface: Someone is cross at being made to dig up and move a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is the phrase that opens the clue, which makes it easy to read as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Syringa is the lilac, or the mock orange, both garden shrubs.

clue.text: At wedding, one who assists our side and the bride?

parts.note: the bride is she, or her

explanation.surface: At a wedding, someone helps guests from the groom's side and the bride herself.
explanation.walkthrough: The ushers at a wedding seat the guests on either side of the aisle, so 'our side' and 'the bride' fit the scene as well as the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher at a wedding helps show guests to their seats.

clue.text: Cleans out revolting government office

indicators.note: letters in revolt overturn their order

explanation.surface: Rebels purge an office of the government they are rising against.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like an adjective for the office (disgusting, or in rebellion), but it tells you to rearrange CLEANS OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A consulate is the office of a consul, a government's representative abroad.

clue.text: Condition that is barely noticeable

definitions.meaning: sounds medical, a state of health, but it is simply a state of being
the surface sense is hardly visible; the setter means noticeable for being bare

explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely noticeable' seems to mean faint or slight; read it as 'noticeable because bare' and it describes being naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudity is the condition of being bare, and it certainly gets noticed.

clue.text: End of play is baffling

definitions.meaning: the close of a day's cricket
a present-tense verb: something that is baffling someone, leaving them unable to answer

explanation.surface: A critic finds a play's final act bewildering.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, stumps is the close of a day's play, called when the umpires pull up the stumps (the wooden posts at each end of the pitch). The surface makes you think of a theatre play.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumps is the end of a day's cricket, and something that stumps you is baffling you.

clue.text: While speaking glanced through mail, very important

indicators.note: the wordplay only works when the words glanced through are spoken aloud

parts.note: the past tense read is said 'red', and a letter is mail

explanation.surface: Someone skims through the post while on the phone and flags one item as urgent.
explanation.walkthrough: Past-tense read is pronounced like the colour red. A red-letter day was first a saint's day printed in red in the calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-letter day or event is a specially important one.

clue.text: Initially heavy duty keeps one sharp

indicators.note: it applies to both heavy and duty, taking the first letter of each

explanation.surface: Heavy-duty work at the start keeps a person keen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy duty' reads as one phrase, but 'Initially' takes the first letter of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective sense: honed skills or a honed edge have been worked until keen, so sharp is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Woman has a fine bundle of papers

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: A woman is holding a fine stack of documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like praise for the bundle but gives only its letter F.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheaf is a bundle, first of corn and then of papers.

clue.text: Diamonds, for example, young girl put on smart dress

indicators.note: in an across clue the young girl is placed before the suit, as one garment is put on first

parts.note: a girl under the age of majority is a minor

explanation.surface: A little girl dresses up in her best clothes, with diamonds for jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: The diamonds seem to be jewels to go with the dress, but they are the playing-card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, diamonds and clubs are the minor suits, scoring less than hearts and spades.

clue.text: Fearful of such a breakdown

definitions.meaning: a plain synonym: anxious, easily frightened

definitions.note: describes the kind of breakdown, an adjective like the answer
definitions.meaning: points to a familiar phrase naming a mental collapse; the answer is its first word

explanation.surface: Someone lives in dread of cracking up.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one thought, but 'Fearful' is a complete definition and 'of such a breakdown' is a second: the kind of breakdown in the phrase nervous breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for fearful, and the adjective in the fixed phrase for a mental collapse.

clue.text: Agrees law needs modifying to show true value of packet

indicators.note: the letters of AGREES LAW must be modified into a new order

explanation.surface: A negotiator concedes that the law on pay must change so workers see what their pay is really worth.
explanation.walkthrough: A pay packet is the envelope, or the sum, a worker is paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Real wages are pay adjusted for inflation: what the packet actually buys.

clue.text: Give the impression of a very quiet listener

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet

explanation.surface: Someone seems to be a silent, attentive listener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very quiet' is a person in the surface but a music marking in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear is to give the impression, as in 'he appears calm'.

clue.text: One may be suited by this second short journey through wood

definitions.text: One may be suited by this

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second
a trip is a short journey

explanation.surface: A second short hike takes walkers through a wood where some might feel at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suited' means dressed in a suit: a pinstripe is the classic City suit, so a wearer is suited by it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinstripe is a suit fabric with fine lines, so a person may be suited in it.

clue.text: Detectives chase sailor to a police box

explanation.surface: Police detectives pursue a sailor all the way to a police box.
explanation.walkthrough: The TARDIS is the time machine in the BBC's Doctor Who, disguised as an old blue British police telephone box.
explanation.definitionFit: The TARDIS looks like a police box from outside.

clue.text: Deprived of exciting adverts

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, and stirred letters change order

explanation.surface: Viewers complain they have no thrilling commercials to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deprived of' ends at 'of', which runs on to become 'starved of': the definition carries its preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, and both take 'of': a child starved of attention has been denied it.

clue.text: Censors prominent headlines

definitions.meaning: banner headlines run across the top of a page

explanation.surface: The censors suppress the most eye-catching headlines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Censors' reads as a verb, but it is a noun: people who ban things are banners.
explanation.definitionFit: Banners are headlines across the full width of a page, and people who ban are banners.

clue.text: Aeroplane makes bouncy noise, full of echo

parts.note: boing is the sound of a spring bouncing
Echo is E in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A plane makes a springy noise that echoes around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Echo' is meant to sound like an actual echo, but it is the radio code word for E.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the maker's name stands for any airliner it builds, such as the 747.

clue.text: Figure cathedral is majestic

parts.note: a stat is a statistic, a figure
Ely, a small English cathedral city, is the crossword's usual cathedral

explanation.surface: The shape of a cathedral is described as imposing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe the grand, dignified bearing of a monarch or a great house.

clue.text: Perhaps Russian editor worked hard

parts.note: a Russian is one example of a Slav
ed is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A Russian editor toiled away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that Russian is an example of the thing wanted, a Slav.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to slave away is to toil like a slave, and both clue and answer are past tense.

clue.text: Minuscule coals were blown about

indicators.note: things blown about land in a different order

explanation.surface: Tiny embers were scattered by the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minuscule' seems to mean tiny, but it is also the printer's term for a small letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Minuscule letters are small letters, lower case, as opposed to capitals.

clue.text: Woman is a bit more needy …

indicators.note: the answer is a bit of the following words

explanation.surface: A woman is somewhat more needy than before, the start of a thought that runs on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 25 down, which picks up 'and a bit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: 'Woman' stands for any female first name, and Renée, the French feminine of René, is one.

clue.text: A despicable man about to pocket one bit of bling?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a tiara as one example of bling

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the letters of A RAT run backwards
the man pockets the I, holding it inside

parts.note: a despicable man is a rat
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A crook is about to pocket a piece of flashy jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'about' is the reversal and 'to pocket' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled headband, an example of bling (showy jewellery).

clue.text: … and a bit distant

parts.note: a bit of something is a portion of it, a piece of the whole

explanation.surface: Continuing 23 down: the woman is needy and also somewhat aloof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit' looks like the qualifier 'slightly', as the surface uses it, but it spells A PART.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart means separated, at a distance.

clue.text: Star name, one adopting fashionable diet

parts.note: Vega is a bright star in Lyra
n is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A celebrity takes up the diet of the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' is a celebrity in the surface but an actual star in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan is someone who has taken up a plant-only diet, now very fashionable.

clue.text: Publicly expose talent I've wasted

indicators.note: a wasted talent is ruined, and ruined letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer confesses on air to having squandered their gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious sense of ventilate is airing a room; its other sense is airing a matter in public.
explanation.definitionFit: To ventilate an issue is to bring it out for public discussion.

clue.text: Daughter is to take care of balloon

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for daughter
to tend is to take care

explanation.surface: A daughter is put in charge of looking after a party balloon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balloon' is a noun in the surface but a verb for the definition: to swell up.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym once balloon is read as a verb: both mean to swell outward under pressure.

clue.text: Gateman finally grants admission

indicators.note: it takes the last letter of grants

explanation.surface: The man on the gate at last lets someone in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' seems to modify the gateman's decision, but it only picks the S from grants.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry guards a gate or entrance.
